questions.question: What is the primary difference between Face Detection and Object Detection?
options: Face detection only works on photos; object detection only on live webcams
Face detection exclusively finds human faces; object detection identifies, labels, and frames coordinates (Bounding Boxes) for hundreds of object classes simultaneously
There is no difference between them, both only locate faces
Face detection uses neural networks; object detection only uses mathematical division
questions.explanation: Spot on! Face detection is a highly specialized task, whereas Object Detection locates and labels coordinates for varied objects like cars, bicycles, and laptops.

questions.question: What does DNN stand for in the context of computer vision and OpenCV?
questions.explanation: Correct! DNN stands for Deep Neural Networks, which is the specialized, highly-optimized module inside OpenCV used to execute pre-trained deep learning structures.

questions.question: Which OpenCV class is specifically engineered to easily load, scale, and swap channels of input images for deep learning detection architectures?
questions.explanation: Great! cv2.dnn_DetectionModel provides an efficient, clean API to import trained deep weights and configs, managing image sizes and normalization variables automatically.

questions.question: What is the role of the strip() function when parsing label files in Python?
options: It splits coordinate strings into comma lists
It normalizes pixel coordinates by dividing by 255.0
It removes all whitespaces, tabs, and newline characters (\n) from the beginning and the end of the text string
It turns on the webcam stream
questions.explanation: Excellent! The strip() method is invaluable when loading label arrays from configuration documents, removing raw trailing carriage returns and whitespaces.

questions.question: Simple Coding Task: Strip all leading and trailing spaces/newlines from the raw string variable raw_label = '  car \n', and print the cleaned string.
questions.task_hint: Write: raw_label = '  car \n' then clean_label = raw_label.strip() then print(clean_label)
questions.explanation: Outstanding! Stripping whitespace ensures that string comparisons match label dictionary indexes exactly.
